description:
FOUND by s538b (probing the exit sequence for #2371).  perl 5.40.3:
  $@ = "x
"; END { print "[$@]
" }                      perl: []      PCL: [x
]
  eval { die "x
" }; END { print "[$@]
" }              perl: []      PCL: [x
]
  END { print "[$@]
" } $@ = "y
"; exit 3;               perl: [] rc 0?  PCL: [y
]
  END { print "[$@]
" } die "boom
";                    perl: []      PCL: []   (same)
Pre-existing (the base 23f0f917 prints the same).  Where: %p-run-end-phase (cl/pcl-runtime.lisp) runs the END blocks with $@ untouched; perl clears ERRSV before calling the END list (measure whether per block: `END { print "[$@]" } END { $@ = "a" }` -- LIFO -- tells).  Probe also the exit status of the third line under perl before writing the guard row.  Not fixed in s538b: outside its members, and its legs were already running.
subject: $@ is not cleared before the END blocks: perl's END always sees an EMPTY $@ (after a normal end, an eval that died, an explicit exit), PCL's sees whatever the program left there
